newsitem.title: USA: Great Western claims Ahmanson avoids vote.
newsitem.headline: Great Western claims Ahmanson avoids vote.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp, in a continuing dispute with H.F. Ahmanson & Co, said Friday Ahmanson has purposely avoided a tabulation on Ahmanson's stockholder consent proposal number one.
Great Western called "absoultely false" Ahmanson's allegation that Great Western has refused to agree to a count.
Great Western added that based upon compilations by the independent inspectors, as of April 9, "it is evident (the proposal) has not secured the requisite majority support of Great Western shares."
Consumer banking company Ahmanson said Thursday it has been notified by the independent inspector that Great Western has refused to agree to a count on Ahmanson's proposal number one.
This proposal urges the Great Western board to negotiate with Ahmanson and place its merger proposal on a level playing field with Washington Mutual Inc's proposal to merge with Ahmanson.
Great Western claims that there is no valid record date for this proposal, but Ahmanson sees no basis for this claim, the company said.
Great Western said Friday the independent inspectors advised both companies there must be a record date established to identify those stockholders entitled to vote.

"Ahmanson has never requested that Great Western establish a record date on proposal one and two nor has it pursued its court action seeking to establish a record date through the judicial process," Great Western's statement said.
"Great Western believes Ahmanson has purposely avoided having a record date set because it does not want an official tabulation of the vote."
